summary: Niels and Richard Brennan review the April 2025 tariff sell-off, Q1 2025 trend following and the passing of Bill Dunn. The second half is a philosophical talk linking trend following to complex adaptive systems and superdeterminism. Main idea: trend followers react to price structure rather than predict, stay humble and diversified, and follow process.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: this whole quarter up to where we are now has been one of building uncertainty
claims.claim: Q1 2025 was a quarter of building uncertainty culminating in equities being pummelled around the universal tariff announcement.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the best time to invest in trend following is at the bottom of a draw down and the second best time is today
claims.claim: Bill Dunn's saying: the best time to invest in trend following is at the bottom of a drawdown, the second best is today (i.e. do not time entry on past performance).

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: markets have to a large extent been driven and focused on directions coming in terms of monetary policy
claims.claim: For 20 years markets were driven by central bank guidance, but now fiscal policy (US deficit cut from 6-7% to 3%, Europe expanding deficits from 2-3% to 5-6%) and geopolitics may matter more than a 25bp difference in interest rates.
claims.indicator: monetary vs fiscal policy as driver
claims.conditions: regime shift away from monetary-policy dominance

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: We need to fade the news, not look at it whatsoever, and just focus on price
claims.claim: Trend followers should ignore news and follow price; they need not retool when investors suddenly have to analyse geopolitics they never studied.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: back in 2010 after the great financial crisis that the market had moved up uh these Elliot wave guys became incredibly bearish again
claims.claim: Elliott wave analysts turned very bearish in 2010 just before a massive bull market, and their grand super cycle high calls can be refitted to any outcome because the method is not mathematically defined.
claims.testable: yes - test Elliott wave forecasts (but subjective)

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: he recognized that these these fractals that give Elliot wave structure, he agreed with that principle
claims.claim: Bill Dunn used a fractal wave algorithm that took the fractal structure of Elliott wave but rejected the wave counting.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I expect to leverage ETF products you know how how how will this financial engineering we've seen in the last few years how does that fare
claims.claim: Leveraged ETFs, portable alpha products and highly leveraged financial markets may be tested in the April 2025 sell-off; margin calls and debt unwinding are a risk.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: 70% of the uh you know, value of all equities are being US equities and a high percentage of that being within the 10 largest companies
claims.claim: Equity markets are highly concentrated (US about 70% of world value, a large share in the top 10 firms) and passive flows force selling regardless of price if investors redeem.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: trend followers would have been long equities um because we made relatively new uh or all-time highs relatively recently
claims.claim: Entering the April 2025 sell-off trend followers were long equities, long dollar and mixed in bonds, so long positions had to be cut, with the dollar reversal painful.
claims.indicator: trend follower positioning: equities, dollar, bonds

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there was short exposure that could have been built up uh in the energy complex mainly the oil complex
claims.claim: Longer-term models had built short oil exposure before the sell-off, and oil fell sharply on the day of the crash, as did gold and silver trends, offering a bright spot.
claims.indicator: oil short, gold and silver long trends

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: My own trend barometer finished at 48 yesterday which is neutral but it has been moving up from very low levels
claims.claim: Niels' trend barometer was 48 on 9-10 April 2025, rising from very low levels, a sign that trend followers were adapting.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: it was characterized in January and February for us in terms of whips saws
claims.claim: January-February 2025 was whipsaw-heavy, with January difficult as the Fed turned hawkish and February seeing commodities (gold, silver, energies) trend; the tariff announce-and-retract pattern repeated whipsaws.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: it's sort of a bit like the boy who called cried wolf, it's happening so frequently now that I think the bounces aren't necessarily going to come anymore
claims.claim: Repeated shock-then-retraction policy announcements may stop producing relief bounces as investor sentiment shifts and buy-the-dip expectations fade.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the models are uncertain the markets aren't uncertain the markets are very definite
claims.claim: Moritz Seibert's point: it is the economic models that are uncertain, while markets are definite, so models used to explain the system for 30-40 years no longer work but trend following relies on robustness over many cycles.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: our ships take a fair while to turn to turn round
claims.claim: Trend models take time to turn so rough 3-4 month stretches with whipsaws are inevitable at regime shifts.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: this massive injection of trillions this this leverage into the market this is what I'm worried about now
claims.claim: Trillions of liquidity injected since 2008-09 built a debt-laden, leveraged system, and Brennan expects a fragmentation of the world order (decentralisation, protectionism) that few strategies can navigate.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Btop 50 index was actually up 16 basis points for the month of April, up 42 basis points for the uh year
claims.claim: As of ~9 April 2025: BTOP50 +16bp MTD, +42bp YTD; SG CTA +16bp MTD, -2.37% YTD; SG Trend +18bp MTD, -4.5% YTD; short-term traders -15bp MTD; MSCI World -2.65% MTD, -4.37% YTD; US aggregate +71bp, +3.35% YTD; S&P 500 TR -3.83% MTD, nearly -8% YTD.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG indices, MSCI World, S&P 500

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: We're reacting to what is what is fundamentally tangible. Price is emerging.
claims.claim: Trend followers do not predict but react to structure emerging from noise; trends are emergent from interacting agents with feedback loops, each with limited information, unlike models assuming an external vantage with control.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: To predict is futile. If we had the world's biggest computers, we might only be able to predict what's happening in the next two days
claims.claim: Markets are open, nested systems of subsystems so prediction is futile beyond a very short horizon (perhaps two days with the biggest computers).

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: It's diversified because we realize these properties of structure emerge from noise
claims.claim: Trend followers diversify widely rather than specialise, because the seed of a trend emerges from what looks like noise and signals identify emergent structure; noise is just complexity we cannot resolve.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: the trades I do impact the market in a slight subtle way
claims.claim: An embedded trader changes the system by trading (larger funds move prices more), so one must be humble and follow a rules-based process rather than predict or control.

claims.speaker: Richard Brennan
claims.quote: I'm not smarter than the system, but I will align with that system and I'll follow the trend
claims.claim: Rely on the model rather than one's worries about news (e.g. Trump); keep trading with discipline because a process aligned with the system matters more than Sharpe ratios.
